_strings.@@07124339f78c: Sales Tax Fairness Credit (STFC) — Individuals who were Maine residents during any part of the 2023 tax year, are not married filing separately, and cannot be claimed as a dependent on another person's return. Credit amount depends on the number of qualifying children and dependents claimed on Form 1040ME, line 13a.
_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@21f5d5abd293: Treaty conformity — ME conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from ME income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the ME return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Maine's resident return (Form 1040ME) starts from federal adjusted gross income: Line 14 instructs "Enter the federal adjusted gross income shown on your federal Form 1040, line 11 or Form 1040-SR, line 11." Maine's only income additions are on Schedule 1A (per 36 M.R.S. § 5122(1)), and the full Schedule 1A list contains NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income — the additions are limited to specific items (non-Maine municipal/state bond interest, NOL recovery adjustment, MainePERS contributions, bonus depreciation add-back, fiduciary adjustments, nonresident installment-sale gain election, and pass-through financial-institution adjustments). Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and there is no Maine add-back, it flows through and is not re-taxed. Maine therefore conforms to federal treaty exclusions (unlike California, which adds treaty income back on Schedule CA). Basis: 2023 Form 1040ME instructions, Line 14 and Schedule 1A (23_1040me_book_gen_instr.pdf).
_strings.@@49e71adfa3af: Child Care Credit — Maine residents and part-year residents (a nonrefundable portion is also available to nonresidents) who claimed the federal credit for child and dependent care expenses on federal Form 2441 / Schedule 3, line 2. An enhanced rate applies if expenses were paid to a Step 4 / Star 5 quality-certified Maine child care provider.
_strings.@@4cf945d1e9e4: Credit amounts/limits are not independently verified: State credits were researched from the cited DOR sources and are not tax advice — confirm each amount and your eligibility at the cited source before claiming it.
_strings.@@4d42ad525021: Mailing address: Some state facts could not be independently re-confirmed — see the pack's `unverified` list; confirm at the cited DOR source before relying on a specific figure/address.
_strings.@@5acdd4c2c323: Dependent Exemption Tax Credit — Taxpayers with qualifying children and dependents (the number reported on Form 1040ME, line 13a) for whom the federal child tax credit under IRC Section 24 was claimed for the same taxable year. Nonrefundable for tax years beginning before 2024 (which includes 2023).
_strings.@@5d83d007759c: Maine Revenue Services, P.O. Box 1066, Augusta, ME 04332-1066 (Form 1040ME without a payment / refund or no balance due)
_strings.@@7d09b15a8d5f: Form 1040ME with Schedule NR (Form 1040ME), "Schedule for Calculating the Nonresident Credit"; married taxpayers electing to file as single may use Schedule NRH (Form 1040ME) instead. Used by nonresidents, part-year residents, and safe harbor residents. (Full-year residents may not file Schedule NR.)
_strings.@@ea078fbae943: 2023 MAINE Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form 1040ME general instructions) — Line 14 federal AGI starting point, Schedule 1A income additions (no treaty add-back), Who-must-file, due date Apr 17 2024, payee 'Treasurer, State of Maine', Maine Tax Portal revenue.maine.gov, nonresident $3,000/12-day threshold
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.
_strings.@@f644a49afed9: Maine Earned Income Credit (EIC) — Maine residents and part-year residents who properly claim the federal earned income tax credit on federal Form 1040/1040-SR (including filers using an ITIN, and filers age 18+ with no qualifying children). For nonresidents the credit is nonrefundable and may not reduce Maine tax below zero.
_strings.@@f8dc8ee216d9: Property Tax Fairness Credit (PTFC) — Maine residents and part-year residents who owned or rented a home in Maine during any part of 2023 and lived in it as their principal residence, and who paid property tax greater than 4% of total income OR rent greater than 26.67% of total income. Cannot be claimed if filing status is married filing separately.

citation.source: 2023 MAINE Individual Income Tax Booklet — Form 1040ME General Instructions (23_1040me_book_gen_instr.pdf): "2023 TAX RATE SCHEDULES" (p. 12, three schedules: #1 Single/MFS, #2 Head of Household, #3 Married/Surviving Spouses Filing Jointly); Line 13 Personal exemptions chart (p. 3); Line 17 Deduction instruction + Worksheet for Standard/Itemized Deductions (p. 4); Line 18 Exemption instruction ($4,700) + Worksheet for Phaseout of Personal Exemption Deduction Amount (p. 4); "2023 Tax Year Quick Facts" standard-deduction base amounts (p. 10); 2023 MAINE INCOME TAX TABLE (pp. 11-12). Cross-confirmed by the standalone MRS document "State of Maine - Individual Income Tax, 2023 Rates" (Sept 15, 2022) and by the 2023 tax tables file (rate schedules on its last page).

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2023 Form 1040ME, line 20: "INCOME TAX. (Find the tax for the amount on line 19 in the tax table in this booklet or compute your tax using the tax table or tax rate schedules available at www.maine.gov/revenue/tax-return-forms.)" — where line 19 is "TAXABLE INCOME. (Line 16 minus lines 17 and 18.)" This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form 1040ME, line 16 (Maine adjusted gross income) = line 14 federal adjusted gross income (federal Form 1040 line 11 / 1040-SR line 11) + line 15a income addition modifications (Maine Schedule 1A) - line 15b income subtraction modifications (Maine Schedule 1S). The op then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (Form 1040ME line 17) and $4,700 x exemptions_count (line 18) to reproduce line 19 TAXABLE INCOME, and applies the 2023 rate schedules to produce line 20. Do NOT pre-subtract the deduction or exemption from the figure you supply. If you itemize (Schedule 2) or your line 16 exceeds a phaseout threshold (deduction: $91,500 single/MFS, $137,300 HoH, $183,050 MFJ/QSS; exemption: $305,150 single, $335,650 HoH, $366,100 MFJ/QSS, $183,050 MFS), compute lines 17-18 on the form's worksheets instead — the op does not model those adjustments. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — 2023 Form 1040ME line 14 is federal adjusted gross income and line 16 Maine AGI = federal AGI +/- Schedule 1A/1S modifications; supply line 16 (the op subtracts the $4,700-per-exemption line 18 deduction and the federal-amount standard deduction). Dependent counts are zero by design: Maine dependents get the $300 Dependent Exemption Tax Credit, not an income exemption. Rate schedule sharing: 2023 Tax Rate Schedule #1 is titled 'For Single Individuals and Married Persons Filing Separate Returns' — one schedule covers BOTH single and MFS, so the identical brackets are duplicated per status (MFS is NOT half of MFJ in Maine; it equals single). Qualifying surviving spouse maps to married_filing_jointly: Tax Rate Schedule #3 is titled 'For Married Individuals and Surviving Spouses Filing Joint Returns', and the booklet tax table's MFJ column is footnoted '*This column must also be used by a surviving spouse with dependent child.' QSS also uses the $27,700 standard deduction and the MFJ phaseout thresholds. Printed '$X plus Y% of excess over $Z' constants are rounded to whole dollars and do not exactly equal the cumulative marginal sums: Single/MFS top-bracket constant $3,686 vs exact $3,685.625 (+$0.375); HoH constants $2,132 vs exact $2,131.50 (+$0.50) and $5,531 vs exact $5,530.125 (+$0.875); MFJ constants $2,845 vs exact $2,844.90 (+$0.10) and $7,371 vs exact $7,370.775 (+$0.225). Pure marginal bracket math (what this op does) can therefore differ from the printed-constant method by up to about $1 in the middle and top brackets. Tax table: the booklet prints a 2023 MAINE INCOME TAX TABLE for line 19 taxable income under $100,000 in $100 bands; Form 1040ME line 20 authorizes computing tax with EITHER 'the tax table or tax rate schedules', so bracket math is a permitted method, but within a $100 band the table (built on band midpoints) may differ from exact bracket math by a few dollars. At $100,000 and over the table itself directs the printed amount 'plus 7.15% of excess over 100,000' (Single/MFS and HoH columns) or the rate schedule (MFJ column). Standard/itemized deduction PHASEOUT is NOT modeled: if Form 1040ME line 16 (Maine AGI) is more than $91,500 (single or MFS), $137,300 (HoH), or $183,050 (MFJ/QSS), the Worksheet for Standard/Itemized Deductions reduces the line 17 deduction proportionally, reaching $0 once line 16 exceeds the threshold by $75,000 (single/MFS), $112,500 (HoH), or $150,000 (MFJ/QSS) — i.e. fully phased out at $166,500 / $249,800 / $333,050. Above the threshold, compute line 17 on the worksheet, not with the shipped standard deduction. Personal exemption PHASEOUT is NOT modeled: if line 16 exceeds $305,150 (single), $335,650 (HoH), $366,100 (MFJ/QSS), or $183,050 (MFS), the Worksheet for Phaseout of Personal Exemption Deduction Amount reduces the line 18 exemption proportionally over the next $125,000 ($62,500 MFS). DEPENDENTS GET A CREDIT, NOT AN EXEMPTION: Maine has no per-dependent income exemption. The Dependent Exemption Tax Credit is $300 per qualifying child/dependent (Form 1040ME, Schedule A, line 8; nonrefundable for 2023), reduced by $7.50 for every $1,000 of Maine AGI over $200,000 ($400,000 MFJ). It is subtracted from TAX, not from income, and this op does not model it — dependents_count does not change the base. Maine's standard deduction 'is equal to the federal standard deduction amount' (federal Form 1040 line 12); the shipped figures are the 2023 BASE amounts. Additional amounts for age 65+ or blindness are NOT shipped because they vary by marital status: $1,500 per occurrence if married (filing jointly or separately) or a qualified surviving spouse (MFS may count spouse occurrences only if an exemption is claimable for the spouse); $1,850 per occurrence if unmarried (single or HoH). Enter them via the federal standard deduction on the form. Itemizers are not modeled: taxpayers who itemized federally complete Form 1040ME Schedule 2 (Maine itemized deductions, limited to $33,200 except medical expenses) and use the larger of that or the standard deduction on line 17 — except nonresident aliens MUST use itemized deductions. Part-year residents, nonresidents, and safe-harbor residents compute line 20 tax on full Maine taxable income, then subtract the nonresident credit on line 21 (Schedule NR or NRH) — not modeled by this op. Tax credit recapture (Form 1040ME line 20a) is added after line 20 and is not modeled. No mid-year 2023 rate change: rates 5.8% / 6.75% / 7.15% with bracket dollar amounts inflation-adjusted under 36 M.R.S. § 5403 (published by MRS Sept 15, 2022; 36 M.R.S. § 5111 sub-§§ 1-F, 2-F, 3-F).
